subject: general
question: In which year was the Planning Commission of India set up?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1950**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Planning Commission of India was established in the year **1950**.
 
• It was set up by a **resolution of the Government of India** in March 1950.
 
• The primary objective of the Planning Commission was to **promote a rapid rise in the standard of living of the people** by efficient exploitation of the resources of the country, increasing production, and offering opportunities to all for employment in the service of the community.
 
• The first Five-Year Plan was launched in **1951** based on the model recommended by the Planning Commission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Planning Commission:**

 
 
• The Planning Commission was an institution in the Government of India, which formulated India's Five-Year Plans, among other functions.
 
• The Planning Commission was set up in 1950 and was responsible for assessing the resources of the country and formulating plans for the most effective and balanced utilization of those resources.
 
• It was headed by the Prime Minister of India and included other key ministers and experts in various fields.
 
 
 
• **Five-Year Plans:**
 
 
• These are centralized and integrated national economic programs. The first such plan was launched in 1951, and there have been twelve such plans since then.
 
• The plans were aimed at targeted growth and development in various sectors such as agriculture, industry, and services.
 
• The Planning Commission oversaw the implementation of these plans.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog:**
 
 
• The Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) in 2015 by the Government of India.
 
• NITI Aayog aims to involve states in economic policy-making in India and is a think-tank of the government.
 
• The emphasis shifted from planning to monitoring and evaluation of policies and programs.
